title: "We didn't want to demonise fetish or BDSM": People aren't dying in horror game Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival because of what they do in the bedroom
description: Early in horror game Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival, the character you play, Aidan, and his partner Sunny, are pushing the bounds of the sex they enjoy together. Already into BDSM, they discover a puzzle box that, when solved, will allow them to explore a new extreme of their fetish play. However, when they unlock the box it summons a set of torture demons called Cenobites and Sunny is torn to fleshy pieces and sent to hell. From that violent beginning, Aidan bargains with one of the demons of torture to find a way to bring Sunny back fo life and made whole. Not your average walk in the park – or, if it is, I am deeply sorry for you. My park is great. title: Star Wars Galactic Racer Has Me Ready To Throw Caution Out The Airlock, And It’s Already Discounted
description: Spaceships are cool. TIE Fighters, the Millennium Falcon, Y-Wings—they’re all awesome, but in reality, the on-the-ground vehicles may be some of Star Wars’ coolest inventions. Podracing is an electrifying sport that looks as dangerous as it does exciting, and speeder bikes whip around like cars without friction. Star Wars Galactic Racer is the first racing game set in the galaxy far, far away in over 20 years, and if you’re looking to get into the driver’s seat, well, you won’t want to miss out on this discount ahead of launch. Developed by Fuse Games, which was founded by senior developers from some of the best racing games of all time—I’m talking about Burnout and Need for Speed—Star Wars Galactic Racer looks to combine the adrenaline rush of a great driving game with the fantastical beauty of the franchise’s most iconic planets. Driving around New York City? Absolutely boring when you’ve got the open plains of Tatooine welcoming you. What makes Galactic Racer even more interesting than your typical racer is the fact that the single-player campaign looks to have gained a bigger focus than many of the largest franchises in the world. Instead of a simple loop that sees you racing increasingly faster cars around increasingly chaotic tracks, you’re more involved, having to climb through the ranks of the Galactic League. You have more freedom in choosing your vehicle, missions, tracks, and challenges, all of which can affect how the story plays out. There’s also a new type of vehicle in the Star Wars universe in the form of the skimspeeder, along with the usual customization you’d expect from a racing game. If you’re someone who’s competitive, then Star Wars Galactic Racer also has your usual multiplayer component, with the intensity that only high-speed races can truly deliver. Up to 12 players can take on the various tracks while you rise through the multiplayer ranking system. Sadly, the Force is not on your side—you’ll just need to use sheer will and the skills…

Owners of the Premium Edition can start playing early on October 1, while the Standard Edition unlocks on October 6. You can also check out our Gears of War: E-Day PC requirements guide to see if your rig can handle the visually impressive game. Are there any Gears of War: E-Day preorder bonuses for Steam users? title: Here’s How Visually Different The Witcher 3 Remastered Looks
description: With the release of The Witcher 3 Remastered, we wanted to take a look at the visual differences using various settings on PC. We compared the game, known as Version 5.00, to the most recent version of The Witcher 3, Version 4.04. All versions were run on 4k, Ultra settings with everything turned on. In 4.04 we had ray tracing turned on, and in 5.00 we had ray tracing and path tracing examples. Path tracing is a new feature exclusive to The Witcher 3 Remastered, which is why we couldn't have it turned on in Version 4.04. We tested the graphics in a pre-release version of the game, and because of that there may be some minor graphical issues. This is something that CD Projekt Red let us know about ahead of time, and something the developer let us know it would be working on up until launch. Keep in mind that anything you see in the video or screenshots embedded in this article may change when the game releases. Remember that it might cost you nothing to upgrade to The Witcher 3 Remastered if you like the look of these comparisons and want to experience it for yourself. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered launches on September 29 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. In other The Witcher news, The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion in 2027. Songs of the Past is the first DLC for The Witcher 3 in over a decade, and is a mystery centered around Dandelion, Geralt's lute-wielding friend.

title: Here’s What’s New In The Witcher 3 Remastered
description: When you boot up The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered for the first time, you’ll see a few new items on the menu: Combat Training, Mods, Patch Highlights, and–depending on the platform–Console Features. Patch Highlights is exactly that. Judging by the trailer developer CD Projekt Red released last month, there are dozens of new additions and changes, but here are the highlights as listed in the menu: Upgraded visuals and performance: Everything from NPCs you'll meet on your journey to the bushes along the side of the road has received a facelift. Additionally, the lighting has been reworked to be more realistic, and path tracing has been added to the PC version. If you want to see how the visuals stack up to the 2022 update, we have a graphics comparison you can watch. Reimagined skill system: CD Projekt Red has taken a pass at the skill system in order to bring more refined progression with greater flexibility. Expanded photo mode: Photo mode has been overhauled to include more settings, poses, frames, and filters. You can also place other character models in the frame. Improved combat: CD Projekt Red has touched up the combat by adding more finishers and tweaking the dynamic camera. Transmog: Now you can wear whatever you want and retain the stats from your best equipment. Finally, Geralt’s iconic fit can be used for the entire game without penalty. In addition to the changes highlighted, other standout features include expanded mod support (even on Nintendo Switch 2) and a revamped meditation mechanic that shows time passing in real time instead of fading to black. From the main menu, you can now replay the combat tutorial. This skips the opening cutscenes and puts you right in front of Vesemir to begin practicing. Since The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt already allowed for cross-saving and old saves transfer, this will undoubtedly be handy for those looking to pick up where they left off. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered also defaults to a new camera while exploring.…

title: "We clearly handled that responsibility poorly": Paradox ban Discord profile pics of historical figures born after 1800, after bust-up with Hearts of Iron 4 players over Atatürk banning
description: Hearts of Iron 4 developers Paradox Interactive have prohibited the use of Discord profile pictures of historical figures born after 1st January 1800, save for official in-game portraits, amid an uproar caused by a moderator banning somebody for using a photograph of Republic of Turkey founder Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. In the same post, Pieper notes that "Paradox never aims to review history or take positions on political figures, and we clearly handled that responsibility poorly." Read more

title: 10 Things I Wish I Knew Before Starting Valheim
description: After more than five years in early access, Valheim 1.0 is finally here, and can be played from start to finish for the very first time. While Valheim’s gameplay will feel familiar to fans of the survival crafting genre--and has influenced other games released in the years since--the viking-themed game has a few unique mechanics that take some getting used to. If you’re headed to the tenth world for the very first time, here are some important tips that will make your Valheim experience so much smoother. This guide avoids progression and boss spoilers. Stay Well Rested Being in your base grants you the rested buff, which appears in the upper right corner as a red symbol. While this is easy to overlook when first picking up the game, having the rested buff up as much as possible is vital to your survival on Valheim--dramatically increasing your HP and stamina regen, as well as increasing XP gain. The duration of the rested buff depends on the comfort level of your base, which can be increased by decorating with furniture, rugs, banners, and other decor. In a pinch, you can get a basic rested buff by sitting next to a campfire, even if you aren’t sheltered. You can also place a campfire in the entrance to a dungeon if the buff runs out while dungeon-crawling. Eat Good Food As in most survival games, food is vital to your journey through Valheim, however the food mechanics are a little different to other games. Valheim gives you three slots for food, meaning you can have three different meals active at once--and you should make sure you always have all these slots filled. Eating food doesn’t directly increase your HP, instead food dictates your maximum HP, maximum stamina, and how quickly each of them auto-regenerate. Some foods give you mostly HP, some give mostly stamina, and others are mixed, giving you many different ways to build your character. Food buffs become less effective as they start to run out, leaving you to decide whether you want to refresh your food…

title: Minecraft Is Getting Its First New Dimension In Over 15 Years
description: Announced today during Minecraft Live, Mojang is adding the first new dimension to the blocky sandbox game in more than a decade and a half. The Sift is an ethereal-looking fourth dimension that was first marketed for Minecraft Dungeons 2, and it's now been confirmed that it's coming to the base game in 2027. The Sift is a major new addition for Minecraft, marking the first new dimension since 2011's The End, where players go to fight the Ender Dragon in the end game. Speaking to GameSpot, Minecraft Dungeons 2 creative director Mans Olson explained that the team wanted to make sure that The Sift felt distinct from the Nether and The End rather than becoming another hostile environment. "We wanted to make sure that it was different. That it doesn't feel like the ones that already exist in the game," he confirmed. Unlike the Nether and The End, where the environments feel immediately hostile thanks to dangerous environmental hazards and angry mobs, the developers wanted it to feel like somewhere players could potentially live. "We thought of it more as a, kind of, different Overworld... it's this idea that it should be a place where you could see yourself living, a place that's a bit peaceful, sometimes maybe even serene," Olson explained. "We already have two dimensions that clearly scream, 'I'm evil!'" That doesn't mean that The Sift will necessarily always be completely safe. In Minecraft Dungeons 2, the dimension is under threat from the Illagers, leaving its ecosystem in danger. "We wanted to make sure that, although it is dangerous, it doesn't feel as hostile or as imposing as the Nether and The End," Olson said. "But rather just be an ecosystem of its own, to be rich and lush and vibrant, and provide a new color palette that's pretty different from what we've seen already." The Sift was originally created because Minecraft Dungeons 2 needed a new dimension for its story, but the developers have been working closely with the vanilla Minecraft team throughout…

title: The Next Minecraft Update Adds Ice Caves, A New Mob, And More
description: Minecraft's next game drop will add a new underground environment to the sandbox game, along with a new hostile mob, and items that bring frosty mechanics to exploration and combat. Announced during Minecraft Live on September 26, the upcoming game drop is expected to follow the usual drop cadence of once per quarter, releasing in December 2026. Its biggest addition is ice caves--a rare underground extension of Minecraft's existing cold biomes. Ice caves are a new underground biome coming to Minecraft. Ice caves will add more environmental variety to cold areas, giving you another reason to venture underground when exploring snowy regions. The caves will also contain ice crystals, which can be collected and used for decoration. Ice crystals can be placed vertically or horizontally, and they'll also produce light, giving you another way to illuminate your creations. However, ice caves aren't entirely peaceful. A new hostile mob in the form of the Frozen Zombie will lurk underground, bringing new combat mechanics with it. Frozen Zombies can apply a stacking freezing effect with their melee attacks. If you take too many hits you'll eventually freeze, making getting surrounded by Frozen Zombies especially dangerous. They can also throw ice balls, which deal damage and knock players back. Being hit with an ice ball will give you the Frozen effect. To create a Frozen Zombie, a regular Zombie will need to be exposed to powdered snow. Fortunately, when killed the Frozen Zombie will drop ice balls. Although if you're not coming across any, you can also craft ice balls. Frozen Zombies are a new variant of the existing Zombie mob. The ice balls can be used as weapons to deal damage and knock enemies back in the same way you would be if you were hit by one. They can also be used to brew a new potion that applies a freezing effect. While Minecraft's next update hasn't yet got a name, you can expect it to be released around late December 2026.
